_comment: Proxyman scenarios for the MedSimQA dashboard.
Import via: Proxyman > Tools > Map Local / Breakpoint > Import.
Proxyman's Map Local and Breakpoint tools cover the same ground as the
Charles rewrite rules, with two capabilities Charles lacks that matter
here: scriptable responses (so a fault can depend on the request) and
As with Charles, enable exactly ONE scenario at a time.

scenarios.name: 01 - Malformed JSON on the case list
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Dashboard shows a parse error state naming a proxy as the likely cause, with the raw body inspectable. It must NOT show a blank grid.

scenarios.name: 02 - Captive portal HTML
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Parse error state. This is the most common real-world instance of the failure - hotel and hospital guest wifi.

scenarios.name: 03 - RFC-7807 503
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Server error state quoting request id fixture-request-id-0001, with a working retry.

scenarios.name: 04 - Truncated body
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Parse error state, not a partially-rendered grid.

scenarios.name: 05 - Slow 3G
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Skeleton placeholders while loading; changing a filter mid-load must not let the stale response repaint the grid.

scenarios.name: 06 - Offline
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Offline banner plus a network error state with a retry. Recovery on reconnect must not require a reload.

scenarios.name: 07 - Stall past the client timeout
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: The client's 15s AbortController fires and a timeout error state appears. A spinner that persists past 15s is a failure.

scenarios.name: 08 - Strip X-Request-ID
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: Error states fall back to the request_id in the RFC-7807 body, so the tester still has an identifier.

scenarios.name: 09 - SSL decryption failure
scenarios.note: Enable SSL proxying but do NOT install the Proxyman CA on the device (or revoke it first). The TLS handshake fails before any HTTP request exists.
scenarios.expectedBehaviour: A network error state identical to a dropped connection. The application must not claim to know it was a certificate problem - the browser does not tell it.
